overall: The AG found no violation: the complained-of December 12, 2023 minutes were still in draft when the complaint was filed, and the other points (vote recording, acronym use) do not violate the OML.

allegations.summary: Complaint said December 12 minutes omitted a list of documents used during the meeting; the minutes were still in draft when filed.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, because the minutes were in draft form at the time of this complaint, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficient minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the December 12 minutes omitted the meeting location; the minutes were still in draft when filed.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, because the minutes were in draft form at the time of this complaint, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficient minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the minutes lacked sufficient detail on the motion to approve prior minutes; the draft was unapproved at filing.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, because the minutes were in draft form at the time of this complaint, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficient minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the minutes failed to record how each member voted.
allegations.key_passage: meeting minutes are not required to include a record of how each member voted unless the vote was one that was required to be conducted by roll call, such as when meeting in executive session or when the meeting includes remote participants.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the minutes gave inadequate detail on a report from the library director; the draft was unapproved at filing.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, because the minutes were in draft form at the time of this complaint, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficient minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the minutes used the acronym 'MOU' without explanation.
allegations.key_passage: using acronyms in meeting minutes does not violate the Open Meeting Law, especially where the meaning of the acronym is clear or discernible
